item.content:encoded:
The two starting pitchers entered this game trending in opposite directions. Gerrit Cole had just allowed the most home runs (seven) in a two-start span in his career, while Eduardo Rodriguez is in the midst of a career year with a 2.62 ERA. One of those trends remained — Cole giving up another home run on a fastball — but fortunately the other trend was momentarily halted, the Yankees scoring five in the first off E-Rod to give themselves enough of a cushion to weather Cole’s continued home run woes.
Cole settled down after the Carroll dinger to give the Yankees six innings, by which time the offense all but put this game out of reach. They kept the pressure on, scoring a further four runs including solo home runs by Ben Rice and George Lombard Jr., to cruise to a series-opening victory in the desert, 9-2.
Rodriguez came into this game with an ERA above six in the first inning and an ERA right around two for the subsequent innings combined. That made it imperative that the Yankees find a way to do damage before the home team had a chance to come to bat, especially with the rate Cole is giving up the long ball. They did just that with a clear disciplined approach not to expand the zone against E-Rod’s curveball.
Paul Goldschmidt drew a leadoff walk, Cody Bellinger followed with a single, and Heliot Ramos also walked to load the bases with no outs. Rice drew the Yankees’ third walk in the first four batters to plate Goldschmidt and open the scoring, Goldy, Ramos, and Rice all working full counts before taking the free pass. Amed Rosario then fought off a cutter that handcuffed him up and in, muscling it to the opposite field perfectly between center and left fielder to plate Bellinger as the runners went station to station. A wild pitch allowed Ramos to score and Rice and Rosario to move up to second and third. This set up a two-run ground ball single from Lombard that just got by Geraldo Perdomo’s diving attempt to atone for his defensive misplay in the 13th that allowed the Twins to walk off the Yankees on Wednesday.
Rodriguez struck out Volpe to end the inning giving him three strikeouts in the frame, but the damage was done. The 45 pitches he threw were the most he’s thrown in the first inning in his career. 33 of those pitches fell out of the zone, but only eight induced a chase.
It’s a good thing they hung such a crooked number, because Cole immediately gave two of those runs back. He gave up a leadoff single to Perdomo before yanking an 0-1 four-seamer right into Corbin Carroll’s nitro zone, the three-time All-Star obliterating it to right for a two-run bomb to reduce the Yankees’ lead, 5-2. Rice made sure to immediately tilt the momentum back in his team’s favor. After falling behind 0-2, he stayed back on an elevated heater from E-Rod riding it out the other way and over the fence in left-center for a leadoff bomb, his 39th of the year, to give Cole some more of his cushion back, 6-2.
Cole settled down to work a scoreless third and fourth, helped in part by a sharp uptick in slider usage at the expense of some four-seamers as well as an impressive sliding catch in left-center by Spencer Jones in the third. He finally began dialing the fastball command to the corners in the fifth, striking out Tim Tawa and Lars Nootbaar on four-seamers to end the frame after Jesús Sánchez singled with one out. This allowed Lombard to restore the Yankees’ five run lead in the sixth, the rookie punishing a hanging curveball from E-Rod by lining the solo shot down the line it left and into the bullpen for his fourth of the year and third RBI on the night.
The four-seamer was the prime culprit for Cole in his previous two starts with a 68.2-percent hard-hit rate and just six whiffs, and that remained the case tonight. However, I believe it is Cole’s rustiness with his secondaries that is leading his four-seamer to get barreled. The fastball still has plenty of velocity — at 97 mph it’s a full tick above last season. I will grant that he has missed location in the zone on numerous occasions which hasn’t done him any favors.
However, after his last start, Cole identified a lack of chase and whiff against his secondaries as the reason his fastball is getting crushed. Hitters being able to lay off those chase pitches forces Cole to overuse the fastball in counts that favor the softer stuff, which in essence gives them the opportunity to hunt the heater when they should be defending against the breaker. When you can hunt a fastball in any count, chances are you are going to do damage when Cole misses his spot in the zone, the high velocity not much of a weapon when hitters’ bats are preemptively sped up.
Indeed, once he started commanding his slider and knuckle curve to the shadow of the zone in the middle innings, the hard contact against the fastball dried up. Having pitched a strong fifth and sixth and with his pitch count at 90, Boone saw no reason to overextend Cole and ended his night after six with his best innings freshest in mind. He finished night having pitched six innings, allowing two runs on four hits with no walks and six strikeouts.
Despite possessing one of the stingiest bullpens in baseball, the Diamondbacks decided that a five-run deficit in the seventh was too steep to justify using their high leverage arms. So, Zac Gallen made his first career relief appearance, the former All-Star in the midst of am injury-plagued, below-replacement-level campaign. He allowed a leadoff single to Goldschmidt and walked Ramos and Rice — again, both in full counts — to load the bases with one out. Aaron Boone sent out Ryan McMahon to pinch-hit for Rosario, and he hit a sharp grounder to first that Pavin Smith gloved but airmailed the underhand toss to Gallen covering first as all the runners were safe and a run scored on the error. Spencer Jones then appeared to ground into the inning-ending double play, but his hustle out of the box and down the line just beat the throw to pick up an RBI and make it 9-2.
Ryan Yarbrough pitched 1.1 innings in relief of Cole and worked himself into and out of trouble in the seventh. Arizona put runners on second and third as Nolan Arenado singled and Carroll doubled with one out. However, Yarbrough struck out Jose Fernandez and Tawa to strand the pair in scoring position. Rice smoked his fourth triple of the year in the ninth but was stranded at third by a McMahon strikeout. Michael Fulmer and Luis Gil recorded the final five outs of the game without allowing a baserunner to seal the win, 9-2. With the Rays having lost to the Red Sox earlier in the evening, the Yankees’ deficit is back to four games in the division, making that looming four-game set against Tampa in the Bronx even more high stakes.
Cam Schlittler looks to cement his AL Cy Young case tomorrow after Dylan Cease suffered his shortest start of the season on Friday. The Yankees ace will face off against Brandon Pfaadt with a slightly more reasonable game start time. First pitch is scheduled for 8:10 pm ET with the broadcast remaining on YES.
Yankees rout the D-Backs, 9-2, who's your Player of the Game?
Gerrit Cole pitched 6 innings of 2-run ball. George Lombard Jr. hit a two-run single and a solo homer. Ben Rice raked with a solo homer, triple, and two walks.

A fun weekend in prospect at Chase – at least, outside the lines, where the team will be celebrating the 25th anniversary of their World Series win against these same Yankees. The main party is taking place tomorrow night, but there are some things to note for tonight. Most relevantly to me who is recapping: Greg Schulte, the voice of the D-backs from their first Opening Day in 1998, through the end of the 2023 World Series, is making a return to the booth tonight. I've no idea how the sync between that and the TV broadcast will work out, but I think I am prepared to handle a little bit of lag for the evening.
With it being Friday night, and since I'm being robbed of most of my usual Friday night entertainment for recappage purposes – no eighties DJ on Twitch, no B-movie about killer hippopotami (they missed a trick by not calling the latter, Hippocalypse Now) – I will once again be tucking into my cider selection. Worked out well enough last Friday night, if my (slightly blurry) recollections are anything to go by. I think I have one untried flavor from the selection pack, plus a couple of "regular" brands in the fridge. You have been warned. Tim should be back for the final series next weekend, both you and my liver will be pleased to hear. 🙂
Another narrative will be taking the first pitch of the game, with Paul Goldschmidt returning to Chase Field. I'm sure he'll still get a warm welcome, even though he is now 1,104 games (including the post-season) removed from the last time Goldy pulled on the Sedona Red. I was looked at the 2018 roster, and there aren't many people there who are still playing in the majors this season. Ketel Marte, obviously – he was the "baby" of the roster that year! – and Ildemaro Vargas, then still a rookie. A few starting pitchers, in Taijuan Walker, Robbie Ray and Patrick Corbin. That's about it, on a quick, non-structured glance. Let me know if I missed any!

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are out West on Friday night to begin a weekend series with the Arizona Diamondbacks.
Ahead of the matchup, New York received some bad news as superstar Aaron Judge heads back to the IL with a calf strain. Yankees manager Aaron Boone also made a few notable changes to his starting lineup for the series opener.
Yankees Announce Paul Goldschmidt Decision
After spending pretty much the entire season in a platoon role and not starting the last time the Yankees played on Wednesday, veteran slugger Paul Goldschmidt is in the lineup Friday, starting at first base and batting leadoff.
He’ll bat in front of Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, and Ben Rice, who will move into the cleanup spot.
Here’s the full Yankees lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Yankees 9/18 P. Goldschmidt 1B C. Bellinger LF H. Ramos RF B. Rice DH A. Rosario 3B S. Jones CF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B G. Cole SP.”
Yankees 9/18
P. Goldschmidt 1B
C. Bellinger LF
H. Ramos RF
B. Rice DH
A. Rosario 3B
S. Jones CF
G. Lombard Jr. SS
A. Wells C
A. Volpe 2B
G. Cole SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 18, 2026
Goldschmidt’s 2026 Season
In his 16th MLB season and his second as a member of the Yankees, Goldschmidt has appeared in 101 games for New York, and across 332 at-bats, he’s hitting .253 with 42 runs, 84 hits, 18 home runs, and 50 RBIs while slugging .458 and maintaining a .773 OPS.
Looking at the Yankees
New York enters Friday’s contest with the D-backs holding an 88-64 overall record. They sit 5.0 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for the AL East division lead and the No. 1 overall seed in the American League.
Currently, the Yankees hold the top Wild Card spot, and if the season ended today, they’d host a best-of-three series at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx against, coincidentally enough, the Boston Red Sox in what would mark a rematch of the 2025 postseason.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees could make a surprising move on Anthony Volpe.
Volpe has had success since being recalled, but George Lombard Jr. has taken over as the starting shortstop. So, Volpe's future in New York is very much up in the air.
New York will begin a three-game road series against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday.
New York Yankees Surprise Anthony Volpe Decision
Although Volpe has been playing better, he isn't guaranteed a spot on the Yankees playoff roster.
After New York clinched a playoff spot, Yankees analysts Bryan Hoch and Patrick Donnelly of MLB.com revealed the likely playoff roster, and they didn't have Volpe on it.
What could the postseason roster look like?
C: Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez
1B: Luis García Jr., Paul Goldschmidt
2B: Jazz Chisholm Jr.
3B: Ryan McMahon, Amed Rosario
SS: George Lombard Jr., José Caballero
OF: Cody Bellinger, Spencer Jones, Aaron Judge, Heliot Ramos
DH: Ben Rice
SP: Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole
RP: David Bednar, Brent Headrick, Paul Blackburn, Tim Hill, Ryan Yarbrough, Clarke Schmidt, Michael Fulmer, Ryan Weathers, Will Warren
The Yankees leaving Volpe off the playoff roster would be a disappointing outcome for the shortstop. It also could signal the end of his tenure in New York as Lombard is the shortstop of the future.
Volpe is hitting .253 with 2 home runs and 26 RBIs this season with the Yankees.
New York Right Now
The Yankees have clinched a playoff spot as New York will be hosting a Wild Card series again.
"Every year you go through a lot, it seems like. But we've been through a lot this year with injuries, with adversity," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "But credit to them for coming together. Through all the ups and downs, they've been a together group. I feel like they've developed a lot of grit over the season."
However, despite clinching a playoff spot, the Yankees made it clear the job isn't finished. New York likely won't win the AL East again, which is frustrating, but the Yankees have confidence they can go on a deep playoff run.
The Yankees are 88-64 and 5 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for the top spot in the AL East.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees' Aaron Judge Dilemma Features a Problem No One is Discussing
item.dc:creator: Matthew Schmidt
item.description: New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge returned from a rib stress fracture on Sept. 8, and it took him all of seven games to get injured again. item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge returned from a rib stress fracture on Sept. 8, and it took him all of seven games to get injured again.
Judge left Wednesday's loss to the Minnesota Twins as a result of what he and the team are calling a "lower leg injury," which almost surely means a calf issue.
There have been no definitive updates on his status since, and it's looking more and more like Judge will not play against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday night.
The playoffs start on Sept. 29, which obviously creates a nightmare scenario for the Yankees. Even if Judge is healthy enough to play.
Why? Because at this point, the three-time AL MVP pretty much has to serve as a designated hitter. Unless Judge has a minor bruise in his calf, it seems highly unlikely that he will be able to play right field if he returns.
Why is that a big deal? Because it completely messes up New York's lineup.
The Yankees acquired Luis Garcia Jr. back at the MLB trade deadline with the expectation that he would be the first baseman. Ben Rice would then serve as DH, as Giancarlo Stanton's status was up in the air then, and now, it looks like Stanton is done for the year.
When Judge is in right field, that isn't an issue. Garcia plays first, Rice goes to DH and all three of those big boppers are in the lineup.
But with Judge potentially having to spend all of his time at designated hitter, that means Garcia would almost certainly get the boot.
You're not platooning Rice and Garcia at first. They're both lefties, and you always want Rice's bat in the lineup no matter what. What the Yankees could have done was platoon Garcia and Paul Goldschmidt at first base given how much Goldschmidt mashes lefties, but if Judge is DHing, that isn't possible.
If Judge is healthy enough to hit, he'll obviously be in the lineup. Running the bases could be another story (just ask Giancarlo), but the more you limit Judge's movement, the better.
That the Yankees have been so mum on Judge's status is concerning. If there weren't a major problem here, they surely would have already said something.
And after all of the experience fans have had with the medical stuff and how New York handles injuries, they know by now that when there is silence, there is reason to worry.
Hopefully, Judge's malady is no big deal and he can head back out to right field within the next week. But Yankees fans need to prepare for other scenarios, and even if Judge does return, that could mean their lineup still wouldn't be all it could be,

item.content:encoded:
Es común pensar en los Yankees como un equipo experimentado en los playoffs. Después de todo, ésta es la octava vez en nueve años que han llegado a la postemporada bajo la dirección del manager Aaron Boone. Y una rápida mirada a algunos de sus jugadores principales muestra una alineación que varía entre un poco y una gran cantidad de experiencia en octubre.
Jugador, Número de Partidos de Playoffs de por vida
Cody Bellinger, 76
Aaron Judge, 65
Paul Goldschmidt, 29
Trent Grisham, 26
Jazz Chisholm, Jr. 24
Austin Wells, 21
Anthony Volpe, 21
Amed Rosario, 11
Ryan McMahon, 10
Ben Rice, 6
José Caballero, 3
Pero faltan algunos nombres en esa lista: El campocorto George Lombard Jr., el jardinero Spencer Jones, el primera base dominicano Luis García Jr. y el jardinero puertorriqueño Heliot Ramos. Ninguno de esos cuatro nunca ha jugado en la postemporada, ya sea con los Yankees o, como es el caso de García y Ramos, con sus equipos anteriores.
Ahora, es posible que algunos de los jugadores veteranos lesionados -- Grisham y Chisholm, específicamente -- puedan regresar a la alineación y enviar a algunos de esos nuevos rostros a la banca o fuera del roster de postemporada por completo. Pero es seguro decir que los Yankees van a contar con al menos algunos novatos en los playoffs el próximo mes, en su búsqueda de ganar su primera Serie Mundial desde el 2009.
Boone ha expresado que sus jóvenes y los recién llegados a los playoffs tienen otra ventaja sobre los jugadores en otros mercados.
"Jugar para los Yankees, jugar en Nueva York”, dijo, "tiene una manera de prepararte para la postemporada”.
Éste ha sido un año de transición en las Grandes Ligas. Consulta la primera ronda del Draft del 2023 si quieres pruebas. No menos de 19 de las 37 selecciones de primera ronda y de compensación han debutado en las Mayores, y muchos de ellos ya son jugadores clave en sus equipos.
"Los jugadores están llegando a las Grandes Ligas a un ritmo muy rápido ahora y a temprana edad”, manifestó el piloto de los Tigers, A.J. Hinch, quien ha dado la bienvenida a la tercera selección Max Clark y al favorito para Novato del Año de la Liga Americana, Kevin McGonigle, a Detroit este año. "No creo que se sientan tan impresionados por los grandes pasos que están dando”.
Para los Yankees, ese grupo incluye a Lombard, quien se ha aclimatado bien desde que fue subido a principios de agosto. Y Jones fue elogiado recientemente nada menos que por Aaron Judge, quien dijo que el jardinero novato "realmente ha evolucionado cada vez que ha sido subido, mejorando un poco más en cada ocasión”.
Por supuesto, habrá contratiempos en el camino. El miércoles, Jones se fue de 6-0 con cinco ponches y cometió un error cuando dejó caer un batazo en el jardín central. Y Lombard no pudo atrapar un roletazo del boricua Victor Caratini en la 13ª entrada que fue considerado un sencillo mientras los Mellizos vencían a los Yankees.
Pero cualquiera que siga el béisbol sabe que los días malos y las malas jugadas son parte del ciclo de crecimiento de un jugador de Grandes Ligas. La clave es aprender de ellos para poder limitarlos en el futuro. Y todo ello -- lo bueno, lo malo y lo ocasionalmente feo -- ayuda a preparar a un joven jugador para su primera vez jugando en el béisbol de octubre.
El mundo está a punto de descubrir lo preparados que están los Yankees jóvenes. Pero Jones ofreció un poco de tranquilidad el lunes mientras disfrutaba de la celebración en el vestuario después de la victoria en Target Field que aseguró otra clasificación de Nueva York para los playoffs.
"Creo que para nosotros, jugamos mejor cuando la multitud se vuelve más ruidosa", dijo. "Estoy bien emocionado por lo que está por venir”.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are headed to the MLB playoffs! But they have a lot to figure out before they *likely* have to face the Boston Red Sox in a 3-game Wild Card series.
A big storyline surrounding the Yankees right now is what manager Aaron Boone will do with Anthony Volpe when Jazz Chisholm Jr. returns.
Since Jazz went to the IL (and Volpe was called up). Volpe has had his fair share of moments, and it begs the question: What will the Yankees' infield layout look like?
Yankees fans may hate to admit it, but with Volpe's previous playoff experience, it might be wise to give the kid a shot in October.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Predicted to 'Dump' Luis Gil Ahead of Playoffs
What Should the Yankees Do with Anthony Volpe?
Has Anthony Volpe done enough to remain on the Yankees roster? Should be play second or third base in the MLB playoffs in place of Jazz Chisholm Jr. or Ryan McMahon.
Over his last seven games, Anthony Volpe has a home run, two doubles, eight hits, 7 RBI, and scored three runs.
In all likelihood, Jazz still has his 2B spot when he returns, but Ryan McMahon?? That's another question.
Ryan McMahon’s career numbers with the Yankees:
🤮 171 G🤮 .212 AVG🤮 14 HR🤮 52 RBI🤮 .636 OPS
How would you grade McMahon’s time in pinstripes so far? pic.twitter.com/cVEPiw5FFF
— SleeperYankees (@SleeperYankees) September 17, 2026
What will Volpe's role be when Jazz comes back?
Second baseman Anthony Volpe (7 games).348 BA // 1 HR // 7 RBI // .400 OBP // .965 OPS#Yankees pic.twitter.com/cqwisk1tw7
— Fireside Yankees (@FiresideYankees) September 17, 2026
Ryan McMahon is batting .210 this season with 10 home runs, 34 RBI, and just 66 hits.
And half of his games are in a hitters' haven for lefties.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Get Strong Jasson Dominguez Message Ahead of MLB Playoffs
Anthony Volpe's 2026 Season at a Glance
While Anthony Volpe's 2026 stats don't light the world on fire, it's fair to note he hasn't been given an extended runway to make a major impact, as he's bounced between AAA and the Bigs frequently.
Across 63 games this season, Volpe is batting .253 (career-high) with 14 XBH, 26 RBI, and an OPS+ of 92 (also would be career-high).
He's cut down on some of the strikeouts, and is still working a decent amount of walks.
Yankees fans, let me know in the comments what you think Anthony Volpe's role should be with the team in October?
If it were me (and being clear, I'm not the GM!) I'd run Volpe out there in October at 3B. It gives the lineup right-left balance, and Anthony Volpe has at least shown a capability of putting the ball in play that Ryan McMahon hasn't.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are officially IN the MLB playoff picture, as they recently clinched a postseason berth.
While the Yankees still have a small percentage chance to win the AL East, they will likely be in the AL Wild Card round, playing the Boston Red Sox.
In such a big series, decisions will have to be made regarding who gets a 26-man roster spot.
One player who is on the outside looking in and will likely be left off is Luis Gil.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Get Strong Jasson Dominguez Message Ahead of MLB Playoffs
Yankees Urged to Leave Luis Gil Off Playoff Roster
Recently, FanSided.com writer Jake Elman predicted a handful of players who will be 'dumped' from the playoff roster, or essentially dumped from the 26-man fold.
"But for now, Gil is on the roster bubble, and we don't expect him to crack the 26-man playoff squad. Clarke Schmidt's return gives the Yankees another depth arm, and Gil hasn't shown that he's worth carrying on a limited staff. That said, we imagine he'd be among the first names called if injuries strike his teammates. "
Gil has pitched just 23.1 innings for the Yankees this season, and carries a 5.40 ERA in that span.
So, yeah, it's fair to assume his spot on the playoff roster may not be safe.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Urged to Make Bold Paul Goldschmidt Decision
What Has Luis Gil Done in His MLB Career
Luis Gil has technically pitched in five seasons with the New York Yankees.
He briefly pitched in 2021 and 2022 with the club, but did not pitch at all in MLB in 2023 before bursting onto the scene in 2024 (AL Rookie of the Year).
However, since earning that top accolade, he has not been consistent as a member in the Yankees rotation.
Across 265.1 total IP in his career, Gil holds a very respectable 3.66 ERA, but perhaps his absence from the Bigs is a product of the Yankees' loaded rotation, rather than his individual ability.

Will Yankees' postseason first-timers prove to be ready for the moment?
This browser does not support the video element.
It’s common to think of the Yankees as a playoff-tested team. After all, this is the eighth time in nine years that they’ve made the postseason under manager Aaron Boone. And a quick look at some of their regulars shows a lineup that varies between a little bit and a wealth of October experience.
Player No. of Career Playoff Games
Cody Bellinger 76
Aaron Judge 65
Paul Goldschmidt 29
Trent Grisham 26
Jazz Chisholm, Jr. 24
Austin Wells 21
Anthony Volpe 21
Amed Rosario 11
Ryan McMahon 10
Ben Rice 6
José Caballero 3
But a few names are missing from that list: Shortstop George Lombard Jr., outfielder Spencer Jones, first baseman Luis García Jr. and outfielder Heliot Ramos. Those four have never played in the postseason, either with the Yankees or -- as is the case with García and Ramos -- with their previous teams.
Now, it’s possible that some of the injured veteran players -- Grisham and Chisholm, specifically -- could return to the lineup and send some of those new faces to the bench or off the playoff roster entirely. But it’s safe to say the Yankees are going to be counting on at least a few playoff newbies next month in their quest to win their first World Series since 2009.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone said his youngsters and playoff newcomers have another advantage over players who are coming of age in other markets.
“You play for the Yankees, you play in New York,” he said, “it has a way of getting you ready for the postseason.”

Yankees manager Aaron Boone said his youngsters and playoff newcomers have another advantage over players who are coming of age in other markets.
“You play for the Yankees, you play in New York,” he said, “it has a way of getting you ready for the postseason.”
This has been something of a transitional year in the Major Leagues. Check out the first round of the 2023 Draft if you want proof. No fewer than 19 of the 37 first-round and sandwich picks have debuted, and many of them are already impact players with their teams.
“Players are getting to the big leagues at a very quick pace now and at a young age,” said Tigers manager A.J. Hinch, who has welcomed No. 3 pick Max Clark and AL Rookie of the Year favorite Kevin McGonigle to Detroit this year. “I don't think they're as wowed by the big steps that they're taking.”
For the Yankees, that class includes Lombard, who has acclimated nicely since being called up in early August. And Jones was recently lauded by none other than Aaron Judge, who said the rookie outfielder has “really evolved every single time he got called up, gotten a little bit better and a little bit better.”
Of course, there will be hiccups along the way. On Wednesday, Jones went 0-for-6 with five strikeouts and committed an error when he dropped a fly ball in center field. And Lombard couldn’t come up with a Victor Caratini grounder in the 13th that was ruled a single as the Twins walked off the Yankees.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees, much like all the other postseason teams in MLB, will have to make tough decisions when it comes to their October roster.
It's a 26-man roster in October across MLB, and no team can carry more than 13 pitchers. How a club opts to round out its roster is entirely up to them, but speaking to the New York Yankees, a recent postseason projection leaves players like Paul Goldschmidt on the fringe.
So, what should the Yankees do with their playoff roster, and who needs to be left off?
More MLB on Heavy: MLB World Reacts to George Lombard Jr. Blunder in Yankees-Twins Game
Yankees Urged to Dump Paul Goldschmidt from Playoff Roster
In a recent piece for FanSided.com, writer Jake Elman predicts a handful of Yankees players who could be dumped from the postseason roster, and Goldschmidt's name pops up:
"Let's get back to the present. Goldschmidt is hitting just .239 with a .680 OPS in 103 second-half plate appearances, and he's only capable of playing first or DHing. Ben Rice fills both roles, and Cody Bellinger can also play first if needed. The one thing potentially working in Goldschmidt's favor is his .313 average and 1.006 OPS against lefties, but that's not enough to warrant a roster spot in our eyes. Sorry, Goldy. At least you'd finally earn a World Series ring if the Yankees finish the job."
Paul Goldschmidt has been somewhat of a solid contributor for the Yankees this season, playing in 101 games and clubbing 18 home runs and 12 doubles, so his playoff status is certainly up for debate at this moment.
After all, not every team has a lefty masher like Goldy who would certainly be used purely as a platoon.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce 2 Roster Moves Before Reds Game
Should Paul Goldschmidt Make the Yankees Playoff Roster?
It's obviously all speculation on behalf of Elman, but he does bring up a big crossroads the Yankees will be at when it comes to a Goldschmidt decision.
The 39-year-old Goldy is also batting .253 this season with an OPS+ of 113, so he's an above-average hitter by 13% in MLB, against both righties and lefties.
Good thing I am not in the position to be making decisions like this, but Yankees fans, comment below what you would do with Paul Goldschmidt this October? And would he be part of your ideal Yankees batting order?

Jasson Dominguez’s 2026 Season
Jasson Dominguez was expected to take a leap in his development this season as the Yankees’ top backup outfielder, but he’s bounced back between the Bigs and minors all season due to inconsistent performance up in the big leagues.

item.content:encoded:
For their sake, the New York Yankees better hope that superstar outfielder Aaron Judge’s newest injury is only a minor setback.
Judge left Wednesday’s extra-inning loss to the Twins with lower leg tightness, immediately raising concerns among fans that he’ll miss the Yankees’ first playoff series. New York entered play on Sept. 17 in firm control of the AL’s top Wild Card seed, putting them on track to host the No. 5 Red Sox in the first round.
If Judge can’t go when the playoffs begin on Sept. 29, then he won’t be the only notable contributor not in uniform during the Wild Card Series. Each team gets 26 players for their playoff rosters, but no more than 13 pitchers. Some clubs opt for 14 position players and 12 pitchers, though we personally prefer a 13-and-13 balance. Additionally, teams can adjust their rosters between series, and obviously they can replace an injured player if needed.
For this list, we’re only including players who are healthy and active as of Sept. 17. In other words, that means Trent Grisham, Giancarlo Stanton, and Ryan Weathers are among those who didn’t qualify. We’ve also omitted Judge because the Yankees haven’t announced the severity of his left leg injury.
Jasson Domínguez, OF
The writing has long been on the wall for Domínguez, who was recently demoted to Triple-A amid another disappointing season. Even if Judge potentially misses the Wild Card Round, it’s difficult to envision the 23-year-old Domínguez returning as a backup outfielder.
Frankly, the entire situation is unfortunate, because neither Domínguez’s talent nor his work ethic has been the issue. He’s always earned rave reviews for his maturity and overall attitude, but injuries — most notably to his elbow and shoulder — have seemingly sapped him of his once-potent power stroke.
Luis Gil, P
Gil has had an odd career, winning AL Rookie of the Year in 2024 despite debuting three years earlier. Injuries have limited him to a 3.92 ERA over 80.1 innings since the start of 2025, and he recently moved to the bullpen. We’ll see whether the Yankees view the 28-year-old as a long-term reliever, or if they’d bring him to spring training as a starter.
But for now, Gil is on the roster bubble, and we don’t expect him to crack the 26-man playoff squad. Clarke Schmidt’s return gives the Yankees another depth arm, and Gil hasn’t shown that he’s worth carrying on a limited staff. That said, we imagine he’d be among the first names called if injuries strike his teammates.
Paul Goldschmidt, 1B/DH
Goldschmidt turned 39 last week, and it’s unclear whether he’s in the final weeks of a likely Hall of Fame career. He’s totaled 65.3 bWAR, and the majority of the 142 players above him are already in the Hall of Fame or will be when they’re eligible.
Let’s get back to the present. Goldschmidt is hitting just .239 with a .680 OPS in 103 second-half plate appearances, and he’s only capable of playing first or DHing. Ben Rice fills both roles, and Cody Bellinger can also play first if needed.
The one thing potentially working in Goldschmidt’s favor is his .313 average and 1.006 OPS against lefties, but that’s not enough to warrant a roster spot in our eyes. Sorry, Goldy. At least you’d finally earn a World Series ring if the Yankees finish the job.
Will Warren, SP
This might come as a surprise, given that we included Warren in our most recent playoff roster projection. But the more that we think about things, Schmidt’s return feels like a significant blow to Warren’s chances of pitching in October. Do the Yankees really need two long relievers capable of eating up innings if the starter leaves early?
We initially had veteran swingman Ryan Yarbrough in this spot, though he might have the advantage as a left-handed reliever.. He also has a 2.91 ERA in 21.2 second-half innings and has since recovered from a lingering right oblique problem.

item.content:encoded:
MINNEAPOLIS — Anthony Volpe bateó con tanta fuerza que perdió el equilibrio, convencido de que la pelota se había ido fuera. En cambio, rebotó contra el muro alto del centro-derecha, un doble de dos carreras que igualó el marcador para los Yankees con dos outs en la novena entrada. Durante un momento intenso y emocionante el miércoles, Nueva York parecía dispuesta a llevarse la barrida.
Lo que vino después fueron cuatro entradas más en las que el equipo llegaba hasta la puerta y se negaba a cruzarla. Los Yankees se pusieron por delante en la décima. Volvieron a hacerlo en la undécima. Llenaron las bases sin outs en la duodécima. Cada vez acababan con un empate o con una remontada desperdiciada.
Un viaje que debería haber acabado con una barrida acabó poniendo de manifiesto el único punto débil que un aspirante al título no puede permitirse arrastrar hasta octubre. No se trató de un colapso del bullpen ni de un rebote desafortunado. Fue la alineación de los Yankees la que no paraba de preparar la mesa, pero nunca se sentaba a comer.
La culpa final recayó en un novato que no se la merecía él solo.
Los Minnesota Twins vencieron a los Yankees por 5-4 en 13 entradas, poniendo fin a ese partido maratoniano con un sencillo de Victor Caratini en la primera base que rebotó en el montículo y se coló por debajo del guante de George Lombard Jr. en la segunda base. Con esta derrota, Nueva York queda con un balance de 88-64, a cuatro partidos de los Rays de Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana, a falta de 10 partidos por disputar. Los Yankees ya tienen asegurada su plaza en los playoffs, pero el título de la división y la exención de la primera ronda se les están escapando.
Una remontada que no llevó a ninguna parte
Nueva York había sumado cuatro hits en ocho entradas y perdía por 2-0, mientras que el lanzador diestro de los Twins, Zebby Matthews, había ponchado a ocho. Entonces llegó la novena entrada. Lombard conectó un sencillo, Paul Goldschmidt le siguió y el corredor suplente José Caballero preparó el terreno para Volpe.
Volpe impulsó las dos carreras, lo que le supuso al cerrador de los Twins, Yoendrys Gómez, su primer salvamento fallido del año y obligó a jugar entradas extras.
Ali Sánchez impulsó al corredor automático con un sencillo en la décima entrada, dando a los Yankees su primera ventaja. Luke Keaschall respondió con un sencillo que empató el partido ante David Bednar. Un fly de sacrificio de Caballero puso a Nueva York por delante en la undécima. Royce Lewis igualó el marcador. Dos ventajas, dos respuestas inmediatas.
La entrada que dará que hablar
La 12.ª es la entrada que los aficionados volverán a ver una y otra vez. Los Yankees llenaron las bases sin outs, la situación que debería haber sentenciado el partido. Pero no sacaron nada de ella.
Heliot Ramos, que bateaba en el turno de Aaron Judge, mandó una bola corta hacia el montículo. Travis Adams la convirtió en una doble jugada 1-2-3. Sánchez se fue con un strikeout, dejando a otros dos en base. Los Yankees acabaron con 7 de 30 con corredores en posición de anotar.
El juez se marcha y el ataque se queda con pocos jugadores
Judge se retiró en la sexta entrada por una contractura en la parte inferior de la pierna derecha que empezó a notar en la primera entrada. Falló dos veces y no volvió al campo, solo siete partidos después de una ausencia de 99 días. Por eso Ramos estaba bateando en su lugar.
El entrenador Aaron Boone describió la noche como una oportunidad perdida, no como un partido robado, y sus palabras reflejaban la importancia del momento en el calendario.
«Obviamente, muchas cosas buenas, pero no las suficientes», dijo Boone. «Ha sido un golpe duro, claro, cuando tenías la oportunidad de barrer la serie y justo antes de un día de descanso. Pero tenemos que superarlo y prepararnos para enfrentarnos a un buen equipo de los Diamondbacks».
Al final del partido, Boone no se anduvo con rodeos con Lombard, pero tampoco lo machacó.
Boone reconoció que la bola de Caratini rebotó en el montículo, pero fue una jugada que Lombard «se espera que haga y sabemos que es capaz de hacer».
Rodón lo da todo en octubre, pero no saca nada a cambio
Carlos Rodón le dio a los Yankees el comienzo que necesita una rotación en la postemporada y vio cómo se esfumaba. El zurdo encajó dos carreras en seis entradas, ampliando su récord de la franquicia a 25 salidas consecutivas en las que ha encajado tres carreras o menos. Lanzó 102 lanzamientos, su máximo de la temporada, y bajó su promedio de carreras limpias a 2,95.
«Empecé un poco lento, un poco tenso», dijo Rodon. «Me fui soltando en las siguientes entradas, así que eso estuvo bien».
Clarke Schmidt hizo su tan esperado regreso en la séptima entrada, ponchando a dos antes de que Brent Headrick dejara a dos en base. El bullpen corrió una maratón que la alineación nunca supo recompensar.
Una primicia para el club que no se veía desde 1991
Este es el dato que pocos destacarán. Ha sido la primera derrota de los Yankees tras ir ganando varias veces en entradas extras desde el 5 de mayo de 1991, en Seattle, es decir, en un lapso de más de 34 años. También fue su octava derrota en la última entrada de la temporada, un récord de la franquicia, y ningún equipo de la MLB ha encajado más hits decisivos en la última entrada en 2026, según datos de Baseball Reference. Ningún equipo de los Yankees ha perdido nunca más partidos a domicilio en entradas extras en una sola temporada.
Lo curioso es que los equipos malos no acumulan cifras como estas. Un equipo mediocre pierde en nueve partidos. Solo un buen equipo es capaz de forzar una prórroga fuera de casa una y otra vez, y luego seguir perdiéndola.
Cómo queda la carrera por la División Este de la Liga Americana
Spencer Jones lanzó su propia advertencia, ponchándose cinco veces en una noche en la que se fue de 0 de 6, lo que demostró lo rápido que se castigan los swings fallidos cuando los márgenes se estrechan. En septiembre se lee de otra manera que en julio.
Los Yankees tienen el jueves libre antes de empezar una serie de fin de semana en Arizona, donde Gerrit Cole será el lanzador titular el viernes a las 21:40 h (hora del Este). No se espera que Judge tenga que hacerse más pruebas. Nueva York ha perdido terreno que quizá no recupere y le ha dado un respiro a los Rays.
Los Yankees saben cómo ganar los partidos intermedios. Una noche en la que solo tenían que ganar uno, no pudieron.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are now in wait-and-see mode.
Aaron Judge left Wednesday’s game early with right leg tightness. There’s no word yet on whether he’ll have to miss time, and we likely won’t have an answer until Friday at the earliest.
Before then, let’s answer some of your Yankees questions in part one of our mailbag. If you want to ask anything else, there’s still time to do so here.
Note: Questions have been edited for clarity and brevity.
Advertisement
Assuming Trent Grisham is healthy, who starts in center field during the playoffs: him or Spencer Jones? — Ed H.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone told reporters Wednesday that Grisham is running “up to a decent speed” in his comeback from a right hamstring strain. Considering Grisham at normal speed is slow, it’s anyone’s guess what that actually means.
If Grisham is ready to go, it will be interesting to see what Boone decides. There are numerous examples of the Yankees opting for the veteran over an inexperienced player like Jones when the games matter most.
Both players have their warts. Neither Grisham nor Jones is a good defensive center fielder. Jones looked abysmal in center, letting a ground ball go under his glove, dropping a fly ball that hit his glove and nearly trucking Heliot Ramos in right field. Meanwhile, Grisham has trouble getting to balls over his head and in the gaps because he’s slow-footed. There’s likely a higher floor of success, though, for Grisham. Even on the balls Jones has caught, there have been instances where he doesn’t look comfortable reading the play off the bat.
So the main difference will come down to offense.
Before Grisham injured his hamstring, he was not hitting. Calls for Jones to take over were already happening. To Jones’ credit, he has produced at the plate. Even after a dreadful 0-for-6 performance with five strikeouts on Wednesday, Jones has a 113 wRC+. He is always a threat to pop a home run, and that wins ballgames in October.
Grisham has one of the best eyes on the team, rarely strikes out and works at-bats. That matters when the batters behind him would likely be Ben Rice and Judge (depending on his health).
Not that my opinion holds any weight, but I’d stick with Jones in center field. The Yankees can always use Grisham, who’s one of the most clutch hitters on the team, in big spots off the bench.
Advertisement
What will/should the Yankees playoff rotation and bullpen look like? I hate to say it, but Gerrit Cole and Max Fried are not looking like aces these days. The team is winning Will Warren’s and Carlos Rodón’s starts. How are these facts likely to influence Boone’s postseason rotation decisions? … As soon as I say this, Fried pitches a gem. Jinx. — Aaron D.
The American League East race isn’t over yet, but the likeliest outcome is the Yankees will play in a wild-card series against the Boston Red Sox. That means the Yankees will only need three starting pitchers for the first round.
Cam Schlittler should start Game 1. There’s no argument otherwise. Schlittler is one of the very best starting pitchers in the sport. You want your best pitcher going in Game 1 to give yourself the best possible chance of not facing a must-win Game 2.
From there, it’ll be a toss-up between Fried and Cole. Both pitchers have concerns attached to them.
Fried has battled command issues all season, while Cole has allowed plenty of hard contact while not getting much swing-and-miss. I’d lean toward Fried over Cole.
As for the bullpen, the Yankees could have Rodón in case the club needs length. The others likely to be on the roster are Will Warren, David Bednar, Brent Headrick, Paul Blackburn, John Schreiber, Clarke Schmidt, Ryan Yarbrough and Ryan Weathers, if he’s healthy. I’d leave off Tim Hill, who has struggled mightily this season, Luis Gil and Michael Fulmer.
What is the realistic outlook for second base next year? Jazz Chisholm Jr. hasn’t played up to his talent, which might make him more enticing by bringing down his cost. The infield is already crowded, though, with Ryan McMahon under contract, George Lombard Jr.’s promotion, José Caballero, two first basemen (three if Paul Goldschmidt is still seen as Giancarlo Stanton insurance), and Anthony Volpe’s re-ascension. — Marco F.
What the Yankees decide to do at second base is one of the most fascinating storylines of the offseason.
Advertisement
I agree with you, Marco, that this season has likely cost Chisholm millions. He is nearing the end of his worst offensive season since 2021. He won’t reach the heights he set for himself entering 2026, but he still could reach a 20-40 season. Few players have the talent to post those numbers. Before this year, Chisholm posted back-to-back 4+ fWAR seasons. It would not be wrong for the Yankees or another team to bet on his upside.
Chisholm still offers tremendous defense at second and excellent baserunning. If his bat gets back to being considerably above average, he profiles as one of the best second basemen in the sport. There are valid concerns about his offense, though. His hit tool is considerably below average, and as he ages and loses athleticism, that could be a major problem that he cannot overcome.
The Yankees should consider giving Chisholm a short-term deal, though. He is a better option than Caballero and Volpe, who are better as role players, and few available players are better than what he can provide.
The Yankees should strongly consider playing Caballero or Volpe, who played a few games in the minors there, at third base. McMahon is one of the worst everyday regulars in the big leagues this season, and there’s a higher likelihood of Caballero or Volpe producing at the plate.
Has the Martian played his last game in a Yankees uniform? — oconnell13
It’s a hard question to answer because you can’t predict injuries. You never know if the Yankees will have to reach into the minor leagues for depth.
But it’s not far-fetched to think Jasson Domínguez will never play in another important game for the Yankees again. He cannot be trusted in the field. Every game matters for the Yankees, and there’s always a queasy feeling when the ball is hit his way.
His bat also hasn’t progressed enough to keep giving him chances to prove himself. Jones has leapfrogged him on the depth chart, and the Yankees now have Heliot Ramos on their roster. There may not be space for Domínguez.
Advertisement
What are the Yankees’ pitching plans for the rest of the regular season? Specifically, who’s lining up for the Rays series and will any of them be limited in terms of pitch count? — Nick B.
As of now, the Yankees are lined up to start their best four starters against the Rays next week. Here’s how it looks:
Tuesday: Fried and Rodón are in line to start the games of the doubleheader.
Wednesday: Cole
Thursday: Schlittler
The Rays are also on track to start their best pitchers for that series. They could start Nick Martinez and Drew Rasmussen on Tuesday, Freddy Peralta on Wednesday and Ian Seymour on Thursday. Their rotation is dependent on what they decide to do for their weekend series against the Boston Red Sox. But if they wanted, all of these pitchers could factor into their pitching plans next week.
Any chance the Yanks consider Ben Rice as the backup catcher on the postseason roster to free up an extra bench spot for someone more versatile (and better than) Ali Sánchez/J.C. Escarra? — Matthew L.
The odds of this happening are close to zero.
Earlier in the season, Rice kept catching behind the scenes. Before games, he’d catch bullpens and do on-field drills with director of catching Tanner Swanson. Rice hasn’t done any of that in months.
If anything, Rice would only be used in an emergency situation. Believe it or not, the organization believes in Sánchez. That’s why they didn’t promote Mitch Garver. Sánchez is out of minor league options, so they’d have to designate him for assignment and risk him getting claimed off waivers. They value the consistency he provides to their pitchers, and they think he’s a better defender than the metrics show.

item.content:encoded:
Baltimore, Maryland.- Paul Goldschmidt conectó un jonrón en el primer lanzamiento del partido, Trent Grisham bateó un cuadrangular de tres carreras y los Yankees de Nueva York vencieron a los Orioles de Baltimore 6-2 el martes por la noche para poner fin a una racha de cuatro derrotas consecutivas.
Will Warren (5-1) permitió dos carreras y cuatro hits en 5 2/3 entradas para los Yankees. Fue una buena actuación para el lanzador derecho, quien había permitido seis carreras en cuatro entradas a Texas en su apertura anterior.
El cuarto jonrón de apertura de Goldschmidt en su carrera y el segundo en cuatro días puso a Nueva York al frente definitivamente, y el batazo de Grisham puso el marcador 6-0 en la tercera entrada. Ambos jonrones fueron contra el zurdo Trevor Rogers, quien solo duró cuatro entradas en su regreso de la lista de lesionados tras una larga enfermedad.
En su primer partido como lanzador desde el 25 de abril, Rogers (2-4) permitió seis carreras y seis hits, elevando su efectividad a 5.77 en comparación con 1.81 en 2025.
Rogers se metió en problemas en la tercera entrada cuando otorgó dos bases por bolas consecutivas que llenaron las bases con un out. Luego, Cody Bellinger bateó un rodado que resultó en un out forzado, produciendo una carrera; Amed Rosario impulsó una carrera con un sencillo al cuadro y Grisham coronó la remontada con su sexto jonrón.
Esa ofensiva fue más que suficiente para asegurar a Nueva York su décima victoria en 11 partidos contra Baltimore, remontándonos a la temporada pasada.
Los equipos lograron superar las cuatro revisiones de decisiones arbitrales que presentaron ante el árbitro principal, Hunter Wendelstedt.
Los Yankees de Nueva York llamaron al campocorto Anthony Volpe de la filial Triple-A de Scranton/Wilkes-Barre y colocaron a José Caballero en la lista de lesionados de 10 días por una fractura en un dedo. Se espera que Volpe sea titular en el último partido de la serie el miércoles.
A continuación
El partido del miércoles se adelantó a las 13:05 h desde las 18:35 h debido a la amenaza de mal tiempo. Max Fried (4-2, 2.91 ERA) será el abridor por Nueva York, y Kyle Bradish (1-5, 4.83) será el probable abridor por Baltimore.
Información: AP.

item.content:encoded:
It’s common to think of the Yankees as a playoff-tested team. After all, this is the eighth time in nine years that they’ve made the postseason under manager Aaron Boone. And a quick look at some of their regulars shows a lineup that varies between a little bit and a wealth of October experience.
Player No. of Career Playoff Games
Cody Bellinger                     76
Aaron Judge                        65
Paul Goldschmidt                29
Trent Grisham                      26
Jazz Chisholm, Jr.                 24
Austin Wells                          21
Anthony Volpe                     21
Amed Rosario                      11
Ryan McMahon                   10
Ben Rice                               6
José Caballero                     3
But a few names are missing from that list: Shortstop George Lombard Jr., outfielder Spencer Jones, first baseman Luis García Jr. and outfielder Heliot Ramos. Those four have never played in the postseason, either with the Yankees or -- as is the case with García and Ramos -- with their previous teams.
Now, it’s possible that some of the injured veteran players -- Grisham and Chisholm, specifically -- could return to the lineup and send some of those new faces to the bench or off the playoff roster entirely. But it’s safe to say the Yankees are going to be counting on at least a few playoff newbies next month in their quest to win their first World Series since 2009.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone said his youngsters and playoff newcomers have another advantage over players who are coming of age in other markets.
“You play for the Yankees, you play in New York,” he said, “it has a way of getting you ready for the postseason.”
This has been something of a transitional year in the Major Leagues. Check out the first round of the 2023 Draft if you want proof. No fewer than 19 of the 37 first-round and sandwich picks have debuted, and many of them are already impact players with their teams.
“Players are getting to the big leagues at a very quick pace now and at a young age,” said Tigers manager A.J. Hinch, who has welcomed No. 3 pick Max Clark and AL Rookie of the Year favorite Kevin McGonigle to Detroit this year. “I don't think they're as wowed by the big steps that they're taking.”
For the Yankees, that class includes Lombard, who has acclimated nicely since being called up in early August. And Jones was recently lauded by none other than Aaron Judge, who said the rookie outfielder has “really evolved every single time he got called up, gotten a little bit better and a little bit better.”
Of course, there will be hiccups along the way. On Wednesday, Jones went 0-for-6 with five strikeouts and committed an error when he dropped a fly ball in center field. And Lombard couldn’t come up with a Victor Caratini grounder in the 13th that was ruled a single as the Twins walked off the Yankees.
But anyone who follows baseball knows bad days and bad plays are all part of the growth cycle of a Major League player. The key is to learn from them so you can limit them going forward. And all of it -- the good, the bad and the occasionally ugly -- helps prepare a young player for his first time playing in the crucible of October baseball.
The world is about to find out just how ready the young Yankees are. But Jones offered a bit of reassurance on Monday as he soaked up the post-clinch locker room celebration at Target Field.
“I think for us, we play better when the crowd gets louder,” he said. “I’m really excited for what’s to come.”
